content:
We reported on Monday that iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users experienced freezing and automatic restart issues after Face ID recognition failures. At the time, we believed it was a software bug rather than a hardware fault.

Apple has confirmed to 9to5Mac that it will release a software update to fix the issue, expected to be available for download early next week.

Although the bug does not affect all users, reports from social media and 9to5Mac readers indicate that the issue is fairly widespread.

When we tested on an iPhone 18 Pro, we covered the front camera while attempting to log into the Passwords app via Face ID. The device completely stopped responding to touch input and force-restarted after a few seconds. Users can then find the relevant panic log in the iPhone Analytics data section of the Settings app.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, with the infrared camera moved beneath the display, positioned near the status bar clock area, reducing the visible Dynamic Island area by 25%.

As we reported earlier this week, some customers mistakenly assumed it was a hardware fault and attempted to swap their devices at Apple to resolve the restart issue. To reiterate, with the software fix confirmed and imminent, users do not need to do this.

Incidentally, Apple has also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to address random restart issues on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
